sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Agrostis gigantea is a rhizomatous perennial grass that forms colonies. Its erect stems are about 0.6–1.2 m tall. The open panicle, often tinged purplish red, is about 10–20 cm long and bears tiny spikelets. Native to Europe, it has been introduced in other temperate regions and occurs in moist meadows, fields and disturbed ground. It has also been sown as pasture grass.

sections.title: Related grasses and uses
sections.text: Agrostis stolonifera spreads mainly by above-ground stolons, while A. gigantea is rhizomatous; identification can still be difficult in some floras. The sources consulted do not establish human food use or a particular toxicity.
